bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (70%+ of outlay) over dividends or buybacks; disciplined approach to pricing to protect market share; cash deployed to capex reduced other income; long-term target: 10% EBITDA margin for Uniclan; no mention of debt reduction or shareholder returns.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical volatility in West Asia driving crude-linked raw material inflation (15-20%); delayed capex execution or cost overruns; e-commerce cost structure permanently pressuring Uniclan margins; failure to fully pass on inflation without losing share; competition from Chinese imports (though rupee depreciation may help); dependency on seasonal demand (BTS, baby hygiene).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined — emphasized long-term brand equity, calibrated pricing, market share protection over short-term margin recovery; acknowledged near-term margin pressure but framed it as temporary; reiterated commitment to capex and capacity building; tone was cautious on guidance but optimistic on structural growth drivers.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 15-20% raw material inflation, gross margin held steady due to strategic inventory stocking — implying strong supply chain foresight; Uniclan’s 8.6% FY26 EBITDA margin is already 115% above acquisition target (4-5%), suggesting superior integration; 4M YouTube subs and 170K Instagram followers indicate a rare consumer-brand bond in stationery, enabling pricing power; the INR30 pack-of-5 pen pricing strategy cleverly masks MRP hikes from coinage issues — a behavioral pricing innovation.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Prudent leverage: debt-to-equity of 0.02x as on March 31, 2026, with net worth of Rs 1,302.1 Cr and cash balance of Rs 61.8 Cr; non-current borrowings fell to Rs 38.0 Cr in FY26 from Rs 105.5 Cr in FY25.
- FY26 cash flow from operations of Rs 254.3 Cr against capex of Rs 292.8 Cr - growth is being funded largely from operating cash with modest borrowing, and FY26 shows net repayment of borrowings of Rs 64.5 Cr.
- Return profile stated as ROE / ROCE of 20.1% / 23.9% for FY26.
- Dividends paid have risen through the cash flow series: Rs 5.6 Cr (FY23), Rs 9.3 Cr (FY24), Rs 15.2 Cr (FY25), Rs 19.1 Cr (FY26); the deck states no dividend policy or payout target.
- Inorganic growth is an explicit lever - the deck plans to pursue acquisition and partnership opportunities domestically and internationally to fill gaps across manufacturing and distribution.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified portfolio across nine product categories and over 4,800 SKUs, reducing dependence on any single category
- Established brand portfolio - DOMS, C3, Amariz, Fixy Fix, Clapjoy, Wowper and Reynolds - with strong brand recall and consumer trust built over two decades
- Modern, scalable and backward-integrated manufacturing network of 18 facilities across five locations spanning more than 2 million sq. ft., supporting quality, cost efficiency and supply-chain resilience
- Extensive multi-channel distribution: more than 130 super stockists, over 6,250 distributors, over 1,45,000 retail outlets and a sales force of over 1,000, plus Uniclan's separate network of 95+ super stockists, 1,300+ distributors and 55,000+ retail outlets

- Strategic partnership with F.I.L.A. - Fabbrica Italiana Lapis ed Affini S.p.A. giving access to a global distribution network and exclusive marketing rights for F.I.L.A. Group products across seven countries
- Recognised by the Pen & Stationery Association of India as the No. 1 Exporter for the fourth consecutive year, with exports to 55+ countries
- Track record of bolt-on acquisitions extending the platform into paper stationery, packaging, toys, school bags and baby hygiene
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and price volatility — Non-availability of key raw materials may impact operations, and price fluctuations in polymers, wood, oils, chemicals and pigments may raise production costs and compress margins. Mitigated through long-term supplier relationships, periodic price reviews, strategic inventory buffers, multi-supplier sourcing for critical inputs and backward integration in selected inputs such as wood processing.
- Supply chain disruption, trade restrictions and logistics cost inflation — Operations depend on timely availability of raw and packaging materials; geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, changes in import/export regulations, global supply chain disruptions and swings in freight and logistics costs can disrupt procurement, raise operating costs and hit export volumes to affected countries. BRSR flags the financial implication as negative. Managed via buffer stock for critical inputs, multi-regional sourcing, extended vendor agreements, a varied base of logistics providers and backup shipping procedures.
- Intense competition from domestic and international players — Competitive intensity may create pricing pressure and erode market share and profitability. Countered through operational efficiency and cost competitiveness, product innovation, portfolio diversification, strategic partnerships and regular monitoring of market trends.
- Product quality and reproduction consistency — Variability in product quality, colour consistency or writing performance can damage customer experience, brand reputation and product acceptance - a direct risk for a branded consumer business. Addressed with stringent standards across sourcing, processing, manufacturing, packaging and distribution, dedicated QA/QC teams, defined SOPs and standardised testing, plus reduced dependence on third-party developers.
- Manufacturing and operational disruption — Operational disruptions or equipment failures may affect production efficiency, product quality and business continuity. Managed through operational controls, preventive maintenance systems and defined safety policies.
- Brand protection and intellectual property infringement — Infringement of trademarks or designs may dilute brand value and reduce consumer trust, a structural exposure for a company whose moat rests on brand equity. Managed by registering trademarks, designs and copyrights domestically and internationally, monitoring infringements and pursuing legal remedies with channel partners.
- People risk - retention of employees and key managerial personnel — Employees and KMP are critical to delivering short- and long-term objectives; failure to retain, engage and manage talent could impact business sustainability and operational performance. Managed through training, mentorship, career development, performance feedback, ESOP benefits and diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
- Waste management and environmental compliance — Operations generate waste, primarily plastic waste, whose disposal is legally regulated; the Company states it is susceptible to fines or legal action in case of violation. Mitigated through a circular manufacturing approach reusing leftover polymers, graphite and calcium carbonate, reuse of packaging, water treatment and recycling, plastic waste handled through authorised recyclers under EPR regulations, hazardous waste through certified agencies and sawdust converted into briquettes.

business.body:

outlook.body: Expansion into 225K direct stationery stores and Kirana channels via Uniclan; new product innovation in art materials and kits; potential to capture market share from Chinese imports due to rupee depreciation; 45-acre plant (2M sq ft) to double manufacturing capacity by FY29; Uniclan to launch new diaper SKUs for margin expansion.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Extend beyond core stationery into a wider kids, children, young adults and professionals consumer products business, treated as a natural extension of the DOMS brand rather than diversification
- Phased development of the 50+ acre greenfield manufacturing complex, with capacity added in sequence - wooden pencils first, then writing instruments, then pencil accessories including erasers and sharpeners, and subsequently scholastic art materials - to align capital deployment with market demand
- Run brownfield expansion within existing facilities alongside the greenfield project to meet near-term capacity requirements; during the year capacity was expanded for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives
- Deepen backward integration so that most key components are produced in house, covering the value chain from design and manufacturing through packaging and distribution, to improve quality, reduce supplier reliance and strengthen operational control
- Build Reynolds, acquired with its related assets, as a parallel brand for young adults and professionals - strengthening the writing instruments portfolio, adding manufacturing assets and expanding the channel partner network
- Scale baby hygiene subsidiary Uniclan by expanding market presence through carefully selected channel partners, driving stronger secondary sales and improving throughput across the existing network
- Consolidate ownership of subsidiaries in core adjacencies - stake in Pioneer Stationery raised from 51% to 64%, and 51% of Super Treads acquired to strengthen paper stationery capability and Eastern India presence
- Leverage the F.I.L.A. partnership for product development, access to its global distribution network and exclusive marketing rights for F.I.L.A. Group products across seven countries
- Prioritise volume-led growth and market share expansion over near-term margin during a period of sharp and volatile commodity inflation, using calibrated pricing and channel margin actions
- Deepen consumer engagement through digital and experiential channels - YouTube, Instagram, creator collaborations and KidZania painting studios - supported by data-driven insights and analytics
- Strengthen people capability through structured induction, functional learning led by internal experts, cross-functional rotations, an expanded Employee Stock Option Plan and succession planning for leadership continuity
- Channel CSR through the newly incorporated DOMS Foundation, with focus on special education and vocational skills, women's empowerment, and two long-term projects - an educational institution and a hospital in Umbergaon developed with the Umargam Industries Association
- Increase renewable energy use, particularly solar, improve energy and resource efficiency, expand recycling and maintain key environmental and quality certifications
- The only capital-allocation intent stated in this bundle is the dividend resolution put to shareholders at the 20th AGM (convened September 03, 2026): a final dividend at the rate of Rs 3.65 per equity share of Rs 10 each fully paid-up for financial year 2025-26, as recommended by the Board of Directors, to be declared and paid out of the profits of the Company. The Board's stated governance principles include strategic oversight and long-term value creation, and the Board's listed role includes reviewing and approving significant capital expenditures and investments. No buyback, debt-reduction target or payout-ratio policy is stated in this bundle.
- BRSR Section B expressly states that at present the Company has not established any specific commitments, goals or targets, while remaining committed to compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations - so no dated ESG target exists in this report
- Energy management and renewable energy adoption treated as a strategic opportunity: a solar energy system installed at the Umbergaon facility supports clean energy use and carbon footprint reduction, with briquettes used as an alternate low-cost, eco-friendly fuel converted from waste
- Circular manufacturing approach: leftover polymers, graphite and calcium carbonate reused in production wherever feasible, packaging materials reused, water treated and recycled, and sawdust from wood processing converted into briquettes for in-house use or resale
- Plastic waste managed through authorised recycling partners in compliance with EPR regulations and pollution control guidelines; hazardous waste disposed of through certified agencies
- Occupational health and safety protocols across all manufacturing locations with regular audits and risk assessments, Occupational Health Centres at the Umbergaon facilities, National Safety Week initiatives, incident reporting and root cause analysis
- Certifications and standards mapped to the NGRBC principles: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, Forest Stewardship Council Chain of Custody Certification, REACH, EN71, ACMI-AP and BIS standard IS 9873: Part 1: 2019
- All nine NGRBC principles covered by Board-approved policies that have been translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners, including an Environment Policy, Responsible Supply Chain Policy, Human Rights Policy, Stakeholder Engagement Policy, CSR Policy, Risk Management Policy and Whistle Blower and Vigil Mechanism
- Managing Director Santosh Raveshia is the highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the business responsibility policies; sustainability-specific responsibilities are delegated to the Risk Management Committee, Stakeholder Relationship Committee and CSR Committee, with the Audit Committee overseeing statutory compliance on a quarterly or need basis and policies reviewed annually
- Independent external assurance of policy working has not been carried out - the Company states it conducts internal assessments instead
- Human capital: permanent workforce of over 13,000 employees as of March 31, 2026, with over 53% women and more than 38 differently abled individuals employed; ESOPs granted to 162 employees during the year in addition to those granted in 2024-25, alongside leadership succession planning and an internal talent pipeline
- Risk management policy formulated in compliance with Regulation 17(9)(b) and Regulation 21 of SEBI LODR Regulations and the Companies Act, 2013, covering operational, compliance and sustainability-related risks
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The centrepiece of DOMS' expansion is a 50+ acre greenfield manufacturing complex being developed in phases. The Company has taken possession of the first two buildings, and commercial production is expected to commence towards the end of the second quarter of financial year 2026-27; prolonged and unseasonal monsoon conditions caused a marginal construction delay during the year. Capacity addition at the greenfield complex will commence with wooden pencils, followed by writing instruments, then pencil accessories including erasers and sharpeners, and subsequently scholastic art materials, a phased approach intended to keep capital deployment and asset utilisation efficient while retaining flexibility against changing demand. Management describes the commissioning of this project as a key priority and expects it to enhance operational flexibility, strengthen manufacturing capabilities and support the next phase of growth. Alongside the greenfield build, ongoing brownfield expansion within existing facilities supports near-term capacity requirements: during the year the Company expanded manufacturing capacity for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives, and made investments across moulding operations, writing instruments, paper stationery and adhesive manufacturing while modernising key manufacturing processes. Capital expenditure during the year was directed towards the phased development of the greenfield facility together with these in-plant capacity additions. The acquisition of Super Treads Private Limited further enhanced paper stationery manufacturing capacity and improved the Company's ability to serve Eastern India. The Company retains a future expansion land bank of 61+ acres and reports a manufacturing footprint of 18 facilities spanning more than 2 million sq. ft. across five locations, with 55+ acres of operations area (as on June 30, 2026). Backward integration continues to deepen, with most key components produced in house so the Company oversees the value chain from design and manufacturing through packaging and distribution. Separately, DOMS has approved a 50:50 joint venture with Seven SpA, part of the F.I.L.A. Group ecosystem, to manufacture premium backpacks, bags and pencil cases, combining Seven's design expertise with DOMS' manufacturing capabilities; it is expected to support export growth and enable premium back-to-school products in the domestic market. BRSR Principle 2 notes capital expenditure incurred towards fire safety systems, sewage treatment plants, water sanitation facilities and electrical infrastructure across facilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic business anchors performance, contributing 87.5% of gross product sales, with exports at 12.5% and recording steady double-digit growth
- GST rate rationalisation announced in the Union Budget is expected to support consumer demand and accelerate the shift towards the organised sector, a favourable backdrop for trusted branded players
- Categories supported by capacity expansions recorded particularly strong momentum, while established categories delivered through product enhancements and improved average selling prices
- Healthy demand recorded across Office Supplies, Kits and Combos, Hobby and Craft, Paper Stationery and Back to School, supported by new capacity additions and new product launches
- Baby hygiene saw a significant uptick, driven by growing diaper demand and enhanced capacity versus last year
- EBITDA margin moderation versus FY2024-25 was primarily attributable to the higher contribution of Uniclan to consolidated operations; PAT margin was impacted by lower finance income from higher utilisation of funds towards capital expenditure
- Intercompany exports were impacted during the year by US tariff actions and softer demand in Europe; the easing of tariffs and development of new capacity provide a positive outlook
- Input costs linked to crude derivatives have risen since the beginning of the year, met with calibrated pricing and channel margin actions
- Operating environment remains influenced by geopolitical developments and volatility in raw material prices
- Immediate priority is uninterrupted manufacturing operations and supply chain continuity while carefully managing cost pressures
- Indian stationery demand supported by rising literacy, school and college enrolment (NEP 2020, Right to Education), higher disposable income, urbanisation and government education spending
- Rapid growth of e-commerce and quick-commerce is expanding stationery accessibility across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
- Premiumisation and personalisation of stationery are lifting demand for branded, customised and design-oriented products
- GST exemption on pencils, erasers and exercise books lowers the cost of basic learning materials
- Government procurement via GeM and state student-welfare kit schemes (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh) create recurring bulk procurement demand
- Intense competition among established brands and emerging players remains a significant challenge for the Indian stationery market
- The Indian school bags segment lacks credible widely recognised brands, giving new entrants a large penetration opportunity
- Indian diaper market is shifting from episodic use to routine hygiene consumption, aided by rising middle-class incomes, retail expansion and e-commerce reach into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: DOMS delivered 21.6% FY26 revenue growth driven by new product launches and strong domestic demand, but EBITDA margin compressed to 17.3% due to Uniclan's higher e-commerce costs and 15-20% raw material inflation, with calibrated 4-5% pricing actions taken; the company is investing INR250-275cr in FY27 capex to double manufacturing footprint and maintain market share amid volatility, positioning for sustained growth despite near-term margin pressure.

open.item: Commercial production at the approximately 50+ acre phased manufacturing facility, whose first two buildings have been taken into possession, is expected to commence towards the end of the second quarter of financial year 2026-27.
The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.65 per equity share of Rs 10 each for financial year 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, to be paid on or before October 02, 2026.

Commercial production from the first building of the 50+ acre greenfield manufacturing complex is expected to commence in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27, after a marginal construction delay caused by prolonged and unseasonal monsoon conditions.

Commercial production at the 50+ acre greenfield expansion project, whose first two buildings have been taken into possession, is expected to commence towards the end of the second quarter of financial year 2026-27.
The Company is targeting consolidated revenue growth of 18% to 20% in financial year 2026-27.

Management flagged that input costs linked to crude derivatives have risen since the beginning of the year and that the operating environment remains influenced by geopolitical developments and volatility in raw material prices.
The immediate priority is to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and supply chain continuity while carefully managing cost pressures.

Build Reynolds - acquired under an Asset Purchase Agreement with Reynolds Pens India Pvt. Ltd. and its global affiliates for worldwide and perpetual ownership of the brand and related assets - as a parallel brand focused on young adults and professionals, extending it across multiple categories and expanding the channel partner network in writing instruments.
For baby hygiene subsidiary Uniclan, expand market presence through carefully selected channel partners while driving stronger secondary sales and improving throughput across the existing network.

At the greenfield manufacturing complex, capacity addition will commence with wooden pencils, followed by writing instruments, pencil accessories including erasers and sharpeners, and subsequently scholastic art materials.

Ongoing brownfield expansion initiatives within existing facilities continue to enhance manufacturing capacity to support near-term capacity requirements; during the year capacity was expanded for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives.

During uncertain times the Company has prioritised volume-led growth and market share expansion over near-term margin considerations amid sharp and volatile commodity inflation, responding to rising crude-derivative input costs through calibrated pricing and channel margin actions.

Build the acquired Reynolds brand as a parallel brand focused on young adults and professionals, introducing products across multiple categories under it while expanding the channel partner network in writing instruments.

For Uniclan, the strategy remains centred on expanding market presence through carefully selected channel partners while driving stronger secondary sales and improving throughput across the existing network.

The Company is undertaking capital investments to expand capacity within its existing facilities and modernise key processes, having expanded capacity during the year for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives.

DOMS has approved a 50:50 joint venture with Seven SpA, part of the F.I.L.A. Group ecosystem, to manufacture premium backpacks, bags and pencil cases, expected to support export growth and introduce premium back-to-school products in the domestic market.

risks.note: Non-availability of key raw materials may impact operations, and price fluctuations in polymers, wood, oils, chemicals and pigments may raise production costs and compress margins. Mitigated through long-term supplier relationships, periodic price reviews, strategic inventory buffers, multi-supplier sourcing for critical inputs and backward integration in selected inputs such as wood processing.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility

risks.note: Operations depend on timely availability of raw and packaging materials; geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, changes in import/export regulations, global supply chain disruptions and swings in freight and logistics costs can disrupt procurement, raise operating costs and hit export volumes to affected countries. BRSR flags the financial implication as negative. Managed via buffer stock for critical inputs, multi-regional sourcing, extended vendor agreements, a varied base of logistics providers and backup shipping procedures.
risks.risk: Supply chain disruption, trade restrictions and logistics cost inflation

risks.note: Competitive intensity may create pricing pressure and erode market share and profitability. Countered through operational efficiency and cost competitiveness, product innovation, portfolio diversification, strategic partnerships and regular monitoring of market trends.
risks.risk: Intense competition from domestic and international players

risks.note: Variability in product quality, colour consistency or writing performance can damage customer experience, brand reputation and product acceptance - a direct risk for a branded consumer business. Addressed with stringent standards across sourcing, processing, manufacturing, packaging and distribution, dedicated QA/QC teams, defined SOPs and standardised testing, plus reduced dependence on third-party developers.

Operational disruptions or equipment failures may affect production efficiency, product quality and business continuity. Managed through operational controls, preventive maintenance systems and defined safety policies.

Infringement of trademarks or designs may dilute brand value and reduce consumer trust, a structural exposure for a company whose moat rests on brand equity. Managed by registering trademarks, designs and copyrights domestically and internationally, monitoring infringements and pursuing legal remedies with channel partners.
risks.risk: Brand protection and intellectual property infringement

risks.note: Employees and KMP are critical to delivering short- and long-term objectives; failure to retain, engage and manage talent could impact business sustainability and operational performance. Managed through training, mentorship, career development, performance feedback, ESOP benefits and diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
risks.risk: People risk - retention of employees and key managerial personnel

risks.note: Operations generate waste, primarily plastic waste, whose disposal is legally regulated; the Company states it is susceptible to fines or legal action in case of violation. Mitigated through a circular manufacturing approach reusing leftover polymers, graphite and calcium carbonate, reuse of packaging, water treatment and recycling, plastic waste handled through authorised recyclers under EPR regulations, hazardous waste through certified agencies and sawdust converted into briquettes.
